name: MacDhun-lèibhe, Uilleam

attributes.attribute: wrote poems of the Highland clearances
published Vindication of the Celtic Character in 1850
composed the anti-clearance poem Fios thun a' Bhàird

text: MacDhun-lèibhe, Uilleam lived from 1808 to 1870. He ranks with Màiri Mhòr nan Oran as a noted Gaelic poet and nationalist. His prose found its first outlet before his verse. His history of Scotland Alba and his 1850 Vindication show him as a strong partisan. He accused the Clearances of destroying Gaelic culture, linking that loss to mass emigration and the Jacobite cause. In his verse he turned his sympathies into song, yet his output proved uneven in quality. His most forceful lines cluster in his battle pieces and laments. He was born a Catholic and trained in law before turning to poetry. His chief books are Alba and the Vindication of 1850.

okr.objective: Document the life and nationalist verse of the Gaelic poet MacDhun-lèibhe, Uilleam.
